newsitem.title: USA: AT&T offers data over mobile phones.
newsitem.headline: AT&T offers data over mobile phones.

text.p: AT&T Corp on Monday said it offered PocketNet, a service for wireless subscribers to see and respond to electronic mail and other corporate information while out of the office.
AT&T PocketNet services can forward documents to a fax machine for printout and access the Internet for information such as stock quotes, weather forecasts and phone directories.
Users need an AT&T PocketNet phone or a compatible phone such as Samsung Electronics Co Ltd's Duett and Mitsubishi Electric Corp's MobileAccess.
The basic service costs $40 a month, which includes an e-mail account and e-mail address, a 500 kilobyte allowance of data transactions and 20 fax pages per month.

Both analog cellular voice and AT&T PocketNet service must be activated for each phone. The one-time activation fee for AT&T PocketNet service is $45 per user. Cellular voice service fees and activation charges are not included, AT&T said. ((-- New York Newsrom 212 859 1610))
